authoring_artifact_selection.detail: The shared contract selects owner by requested output: requirement markdown, selected production/entity/adapter/formal test spec, selected CBF/SWF file set, scenario-only design, or an unresolved architecture decision. All three authoring skills reference the same contract and retain their separate output schemas and source-binding constraints.

formal_test_spec_and_gwt.detail: A formal test specification remains a spec-author artifact even when it contains GWT. Scenario notes or assertion design route to bdd-gwt-test-designer; that design remains input, not test implementation authority.

code_only_problem_frame.detail: Problem-frame authoring accepts explicitly scoped code/test observations when normative documents do not exist, requires observed/inferred labeling and open questions, selects exactly one CBF or SWF file set, and does not claim compliance.

local_radius_and_generic_slice.detail: A local change is selected by one target, operation, and bounded direct radius rather than file count. New class/interface work is outside local-change; an accepted bounded design can use slice-implementer's generic mode without reopening architecture.

architecture_authorization_and_effective.detail: Missing or changed responsibility, dependency direction, aggregate boundary, business language, or compatibility decision still routes to architecture. Authoring and implementation do not manufacture authorization, compliance, or effective-rule satisfaction; each skill retains its resolver-backed gate.

identity_wrappers_roles_and_historical_c.detail: The registry retains all five canonical identities and their existing capability slots. Codex and Claude wrappers remain thin pointers to their canonical specs. Existing role bindings and schemas remain referenced rather than replaced.

retained_reference_and_core_package_surf.detail: Targeted scans of the five skill trees, shared contracts, profile mapping, wrappers, and guides found no contradictory retained wording. The delta does not change machine capability mappings, package profile data, or core-only routing code. Static inspection cannot prove package closure; the parent runs that validation separately.
